1 big thing: Americans' food faith plummets
 
Data: Gallup. Chart: Avery Lotz/Axios

Americans' confidence in food safety has plummeted to new lows amid several high-profile recalls, Axios' Avery Lotz reports from a new Gallup poll.

By the numbers: Less than half of U.S. adults say they have a great deal (11%) or a fair amount (36%) of confidence in the federal government to ensure food safety, according to the poll, which was conducted last month.

  • A majority has not much or no confidence in the government's ability to police their food — a first in Gallup's poll, which has been conducted intermittently for over two decades.

🛒 Americans' confidence in food sold at grocery stores has also dropped, falling to a record low of 65% saying they are somewhat or very confident.

  • That's down from 81% in 2019.

🖼️ The big picture: This summer saw a flurry of overlapping recalls and FDA investigations, while health experts warned that Trump administration cuts had weakened public health and food safety infrastructure.

  • Gallup's poll was conducted around the time the federal government declared the end to an outbreak of cyclospora, a parasite that caused stomach illnesses, two deaths and more than 500 hospitalizations across 21 states.

2. ☕️🌯 Report: Starbucks mulls Chipotle bid
 
Illustration: Aïda Amer/Axios

Chipotle shares jumped today after the Financial Times reported that Starbucks has considered acquiring the burrito chain, Axios' Nathan Bomey writes.

  • It's unclear whether an offer has been made or if it's just under consideration.

Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol was widely credited with turning around Chipotle before taking on his current job, where he's been tasked with another revival effort.

  • The move would rank as the biggest acquisition in the history of the restaurant industry by a long shot, topping Burger King's $11 billion deal for Tim Hortons in 2014.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 

Image: NOAA
 
  1. 🌊 Forecasters expect Hurricane Isaias to strengthen before making landfall late Friday or early Saturday along the Gulf Coast. Hurricane and storm surge warnings are in effect across the area, and damaging winds could trigger power outages. Latest forecast.

Vice President JD Vance said today: "Our message to Microsoft is, you're a great American company, but you've got to hire great American workers." Go deeper.
  4. 📚 Canadian poet, essayist and translator Anne Carson won the Nobel Prize in literature for playful, genre-blending works that fuse the classical and the modern. Carson said she was in Iceland "listening to the wind" when she got the news. Go deeper.
 
 
4. 📺 1 for the road: What to watch this weekend
 
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios. Stock: Getty Images

Whether you crave horror, thriller, comedy or sci-fi, there's a new streaming pick for you this weekend, Axios' Carly Mallenbaum writes.

😱 Carrie (Prime Video)

  • Mike Flanagan's adaptation of Stephen King's novel follows Carrie White (Summer H. Howell), a sheltered teen who faces a viral bullying scandal at her new school and discovers telekinetic powers.

👽 Disclosure Day (Peacock)

  • A Kansas City meteorologist (Emily Blunt) and a cybersecurity whistleblower (Josh O'Connor) race to reveal evidence of extraterrestrial life and a decades-long cover-up.

🪄 Small Prophets (Apple TV)

  • Seven years after his partner Clea disappears, Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley) follows an alchemy recipe his father gave him to create magical spirits that can predict the future.
